questions.question: Which statement about Spring and Spring Boot is correct?
options: Spring Boot replaced the Spring Framework in 2014
Spring Boot is a separate framework with its own annotations for everything
Spring Boot is built on the Spring Framework and sets it up for you
Spring Boot can only be used without the Spring Framework
questions.explanation: Spring Boot sits on top of Spring and configures it; the core features still come from the Spring Framework.

questions.question: Which of these annotations comes from the Spring Framework itself, not from Spring Boot?
options: @RestController
@SpringBootApplication
@EnableAutoConfiguration
@SpringBootTest
questions.explanation: @RestController is part of Spring MVC in the Spring Framework; the other three are Spring Boot annotations.

questions.question: A plain Spring app is packaged as cinego-plain.war and copied into Tomcat on port 8080. Its controller has @GetMapping("/shows"). Which URL returns the shows?
options: http://localhost:8080/shows
http://localhost:8080/webapps/cinego-plain/shows
http://localhost:8080/cinego-plain.war/shows
http://localhost:8080/cinego-plain/shows
questions.explanation: Tomcat uses the WAR file name, cinego-plain, as the context path, so the path is /cinego-plain/shows.

questions.question: A plain Spring app has WebConfig with @Configuration and @EnableWebMvc, an AppInitializer and a @RestController, but every request returns 404. What is the most likely bug?
options: Tomcat does not support @RestController
WebConfig has no @ComponentScan, so the controller is never created
The controller method must return a String
The app needs @SpringBootApplication to handle requests
questions.explanation: Without @ComponentScan, Spring never finds the controller class, so no handler exists for the path.

questions.question: What does Spring Boot's embedded server change about running a web app?
options: You no longer need Java installed
Your app can only run inside an IDE
You run one JAR that starts its own Tomcat instead of deploying a WAR to a separate server
Every request is handled without Spring MVC
questions.explanation: With an embedded server, the web server lives inside your app, so java -jar starts everything.
